whatThePageStates: The page introduces GuardDuty attack sequence findings, which fire when a correlated group of signals matches a suspicious sequence, and then publishes the catalogue of those finding types. A Topics list names five finding types, and the body has exactly five H2 sections, one per type: AttackSequence:EKS/CompromisedCluster, AttackSequence:ECS/CompromisedCluster, AttackSequence:EC2/CompromisedInstanceGroup, AttackSequence:IAM/CompromisedCredentials and AttackSequence:S3/CompromisedData. Each section carries a one-sentence description heading, a default severity bullet (Critical in all five), a data-sources bullet, prose about the correlation algorithm, and remediation links. There is no table, no Yes/No column, no per-Region or per-plan matrix, and no statement anywhere that some sequence is NOT detected. Coverage is therefore purely a published catalogue: five types exist, everything else is absent rather than denied.

features.statuses: 5 supported (present in the catalogue), 0 explicitly not-supported, 0 partial; 5+0+0=5. Every H2 section on the page names a finding type that GuardDuty generates, so presence is the only status the page expresses. There is no No column, no 'isn't available' sentence and no exclusion note, so nothing on this page may be counted as a stated non-support. The five come from five '## AttackSequence:...' headings, which match the five Topics bullets one-to-one.
features.scope: None. The page states no Region list, no partition, no GuardDuty protection-plan enablement matrix and no per-account or per-tier qualification for these five types. The data-source links per type are inputs the correlation uses, not a scope dimension the page varies coverage over.
features.reasoning: The unit of claim is the finding type identifier — the thing AWS names, gives a default severity, and tells you how to remediate. It is a catalogue axis because the list of AttackSequence:* identifiers exists only because GuardDuty publishes it; there is no independent universe of attack sequences to check coverage against. Counting anything finer (severity bullets, data-source bullets, remediation paragraphs) would count attributes of a finding type rather than the finding type itself.

shouldNotExtract: The 'Topics' navigation list (it duplicates the five H2 sections — count one or the other, never both). The five 'Default severity: Critical' bullets, which are severity metadata, not coverage. The per-section 'Data sources' bullet lists (17 entries in total across the five sections) — these are the signal inputs to a detection, not an enumeration of supported data sources. The description H3 headings ('A sequence of suspicious actions performed by...'), which restate the finding type rather than adding one. The bulleted lists of observed behaviours under AttackSequence:EC2/CompromisedInstanceGroup (5 bullets: malicious processes, malicious files, suspicious network connections, cryptocurrency mining, suspicious use of instance credentials) and the 2-bullet 'compromise could involve' list in the same section — those are illustrative examples, not catalogue entries. All remediation cross-links. The concept-page link for 'weak signals'. The whole trailing 'See also' block about optional AI-coding-assistant skills and the aws agent-toolkit search-skills command, which is boilerplate and carries no coverage.
coverageDimensions: REGION: nothing. The page never mentions a Region, an availability list or a partition, so any per-Region figure attributed to this page is fabricated. SERVICE: nothing enumerable. Service names (EKS, ECS, EC2, IAM, S3) appear only inside the finding-type identifiers and prose; the page does not claim 'GuardDuty attack sequences support these five services' as a coverage statement over an external service universe, and it says nothing about the services it omits. Treating this as a 5-service coverage claim reads a denial into silence. RESOURCE TYPE: nothing. Resource kinds (cluster, instance group, credentials, bucket) are mentioned only as what a finding is about; there is no resource-type support matrix. The only defensible number this page yields is 5 finding types.
trap: The single most likely misparse is harvesting the per-section 'Data sources' bullets as coverage rows, which inflates the count from 5 to about 22 (5 finding types + 17 data-source entries) or yields a phantom dataSource feature of ~10-11 distinct sources; those bullets describe what feeds a detection, not what is supported. Runners-up: (1) double counting the five Topics links plus the five H2 sections for a total of 10; (2) counting the five 'Default severity: Critical' bullets as a second capability; (3) picking up the EC2 section's 5 observed-behaviour bullets and 2 'compromise could involve' bullets as finding types, giving 12; (4) inferring service coverage — reporting 5 supported services and, worse, treating every AWS service not named here as a stated No when the page never denies anything; (5) scraping the 'See also' AI-coding-assistant paragraph as content.
